Let \(\alpha\) be the unique positive root of
\[
3+2\cdot 2^p-6\cdot 3^p-16\cdot 4^p+16\cdot 6^p=0.
\]
Numerically,
\[
\alpha=0.265541219401380\ldots
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{(\wp,\dim E)=(\alpha,56)}.
\]

Sketch of the verification: the flag graph is the chamber graph of the \(A_3\) spherical building over \(\mathbb F_2\). For two chambers, the distance is the Coxeter length of their relative Weyl position \(w\in S_4\), and the number of chambers at relative position \(w\) is \(2^{\ell(w)}\). The distance kernel therefore lies in the \(q=2\) Iwahori-Hecke algebra of \(S_4\).

Decomposing the flag representation
\[
\mathbb R^X\simeq
1\oplus 14^{\oplus 3}\oplus 20^{\oplus 2}\oplus 56^{\oplus 3}\oplus 64
\]
and diagonalizing the Hecke action of
\[
K_p(F,H)=d(F,H)^p
\]
on the nonconstant part gives the first eigenvalue to reach \(0\):
\[
\lambda(p)=3+2\cdot 2^p-6\cdot 3^p-16\cdot 4^p+16\cdot 6^p,
\]
coming from the \(56\)-dimensional unipotent constituent. Since \(\lambda(0)=-1\), \(\lambda(p)<0\) for \(0<p<\alpha\), and all other nonconstant eigenvalues remain negative up to \(p=\alpha\), the supremal negative type is \(\wp=\alpha\). At \(p=\alpha\), exactly that \(56\)-dimensional constituent is the equality space, so \(\dim E=56\).
